annotation.title_clean: Human rights during the mass introduction of artificial intelligence and robotic systems into public life
annotation.title_en: Human rights during the mass introduction of artificial intelligence and robotic systems into public life
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kuteynikov, D.; Izhaev, O.; Lebedev, V.; Zenin, S.
annotation.summary_en: Comparative legal article on human rights protection when AI and robotic systems are used for remote biometric identification and social credit systems, comparing the UK, US, EU and China. Finds that the UK permits tightly limited live facial recognition, the US lacks federal law, the EU draft AI Act bans it with exceptions, and states differ on social credit.
key_provisions_or_claims: UK permits real-time facial recognition in public spaces but limits it through legislation and enforcement practice.
US has no federal law on AI biometric identification; some states and cities ban or restrict it.
Draft EU AI Act bans real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement except three listed situations.
EDPB and EDPS call for a general ban on AI recognition of human features in public places.
States take differing approaches to social credit systems, from prohibition to building national frameworks.
